An MCP tool's `maxResultSizeChars` is `X?Math.min(O,$Ae):ESe.maxResultSizeChars`, where `O=Nr(J)` reads `_meta["anthropic/maxResultSizeChars"]` (accepted only when a finite number > 0), `X` is whether that was present, `$Ae=500000`, and the generic MCP tool `ESe` carries `maxResultSizeChars:1e5`. Its `persistenceThresholdCeiling` is `$Ae` when annotated and unset otherwise. The persistence threshold `rse(e,r,n=bU,o)` returns `Math.min(r,n)` with default ceiling `bU=50000`, unless a per-tool-name numeric override `x(q,{})?.[e]` is set, in which case it returns that override. So: unannotated MCP tool → min(100000, 50000) = 50000 characters; annotated with value A → min(min(A,500000), 500000), i.e. an annotation below 50000 lowers the threshold as well as one above raises it. What `x(q,{})` reads (a setting or a remote flag) was not established.

note: The MCP `fact` reply (`fact_result`, src/mcp.rs) is a JSON object with `id`, `action`, `attention`, `folded`, `refused_since_previous_fact` and `verify`; it carries no captured output. `folded` is `describe_buffer` over the whole pending buffer loaded before dispatch (src/mcp.rs 815-817), and `describe_buffer` (src/facts.rs 392-407) emits, for every pending entry, that entry's full `label` followed by its age — no entry is skipped or shortened. So `folded`'s size is the sum of every pending label, unbounded in both the number of entries and each label's length.

In `look_grep` (src/observe.rs 937-993) the exclusion note from `exclusion_note` is appended to the `printed` return as `({note})` in both the no-match and the match branch, and embedded in the whole-search pending entry's label (`no-match (ERE): … — {note}` and `search: … — N files matched — {note}`). In the match branch `printed` is grep's whole stdout followed by that note, with no size bound. `exclusion_note` (353-390) names every skipped rendered memo and every git-ignored path by relativized name, joined with ", ", with no cap on count. So one search's label, and its `printed` return, grow linearly with the number of rendered memos and git-ignored paths under the searched repository.

Three MCP replies are handed back unmeasured. `look` (src/mcp.rs 781-790) returns `outcome.printed` through `text_result`. For a plain open, `look_path` (src/observe.rs 533-573) builds `printed` as a `==> {path} <==` header plus `shown`, which is the whole file when `lines` is None, or the selected range otherwise; `shown` is then moved into the pending entry's `output`, so `printed` is a copy made before that move. `run` (src/mcp.rs 793-802) returns `{exit_code, output: outcome.printed}`. `query` (src/mcp.rs 1182-1199) returns the string from `query::*_text` through `text_result`. In src/query.rs, `facts_text` prints every fact's id, pin, revisions, note and every extent label; `claims_text` prints every claim's id, status, citations and proposition; `prose_text` prints, per block, its position, id, kind, the first line of its text, its cites and revisions. None of these three handlers or four functions takes a size limit, an offset or a filter, other than `deps`' single `id`.

"Transcribed verbatim" cannot be an honour-system field, and does not need to be: the decidable relation is that a premise's text is refused unless it is a verbatim substring of the cited donor fact's captured output. Both sides of that comparison are Strings the tool controls — a fact's output is produced only by look/run (file bytes read verbatim by look_path, grep match lines, a process's merged stream), no authoring surface lets anyone supply output by hand, and output is immutable after mint — so substring containment is a pure byte-level comparison with no normalisation step owned by the check. Typing is the selection mechanism, not the trust: the author types the premise, but a typed premise the donor never wrote fails containment and is refused at the verb. This is exactly the README's Direction item for supporting-span selection ("refused unless it is a verbatim substring of a cited fact — the author cannot type an extent, and here could not invent support, only select it"), and TET-29 is the first place it becomes load-bearing rather than roadmap.

At d9474d9, fit_findings (src/mcp.rs) chooses one cap for every finding's quoted text: a binary search for the largest cap in MIN_CAP..=FINDING_TEXT_CAP (FINDING_TEXT_CAP = ENTRY_CAP / 2) at which all findings, cut to that cap, fit the allowance. It does not divide the allowance by the number of findings, so short fields leave room that raises the common cap for the others. Only when no cap fits all findings does a second binary search find the longest prefix of findings that fits, withholding the rest.
